araea: The mouth is opened less than for 'ㅏ' and more than for 'ㅗ'. The lips are neither spread as for 'ㅏ' nor rounded as for 'ㅗ', but held about halfway between. The tongue is drawn inward as for 'ㅗ', more than when producing 'ㅡ', and much more than for 'ㅣ', whose tongue is not drawn inward at all. Because the center of the tongue is drawn inward, the glottis opens slightly and the sound resonates deep in the larynx.
ae: An unrounded front low vowel. The tongue is advanced a little and held slightly higher than the position for 'ㅏ', and the mouth is opened fairly wide while the breath is exhaled. It is a monophthong.
eo: An unrounded central mid vowel. The tongue is raised a little, the lips are held in a neutral position, and the mouth is opened fairly wide so that the inside of the mouth is broad. The lips stay relaxed and the corners of the mouth are opened a little wide, broadening the front of the mouth. The tongue body is raised slightly; the tongue floats in the mouth and is drawn a little backward, and the lips are opened a little more than for 'ㅡ'.
e: An unrounded front mid vowel. The tongue is advanced a little and held slightly higher than the position for 'ㅓ', and the mouth is opened to a moderate degree while the breath is exhaled. It is a monophthong.
o: A rounded back close-mid vowel. The lips are rounded and protrude slightly, the corners of the mouth are opened a little wide, and the back of the tongue is brought toward the soft palate. For 'ㅗ', the back of the tongue approaches the soft palate less closely than for 'ㅜ' or 'ㅡ'. The tongue tip lies behind the lower teeth but does not touch them. The sides of the tongue are lowered so that they do not touch the molars. The jaw is opened only enough for the little finger to slip in a little.
oe: A rounded front mid vowel. The tongue is placed a little forward of the position for 'ㅗ', the lips are rounded, and the breath is exhaled. It is a monophthong. It can also be pronounced as a diphthong: the tongue and lips start in the posture for 'ㅗ' and move to the posture for 'ㅐ' while the breath is exhaled.
u: A rounded back high vowel. The lips are rounded and protruded somewhat, the corners of the mouth are opened as little as possible, and the back of the tongue is brought very close to the soft palate. The tongue tip lies behind the lower teeth but does not touch them. The sides of the tongue lightly touch the upper molars. The jaw is closed so that the lower and upper molars almost meet.
wi: A rounded front high vowel. The tongue is placed a little forward of the position for 'ㅜ', the lips are rounded and protruded, and the breath is exhaled. It is a monophthong. It can also be pronounced as a diphthong: the tongue and lips start in the posture for 'ㅜ' and move to the posture for 'ㅣ' while the breath is exhaled.
eu: An unrounded central high vowel. The lips are spread flat, slightly sideways, and the corners of the mouth are opened as little as possible. The back of the tongue is brought very close to the soft palate. The tongue tip lies behind the lower teeth without touching them, while the tongue is drawn slightly inward. The sides of the tongue come close enough to the molars to touch them lightly, and the jaw is closed so that the lower and upper molars almost meet.
i: An unrounded front high vowel. The lips are spread slightly sideways, the tongue is advanced, and the front of the tongue body is raised very high, close to the hard palate. The mouth is drawn slightly forward and the corners of the mouth are opened as little as possible. The tongue tip rests against the back of the lower teeth, and the sides of the tongue are pressed firmly against the upper molars. The jaw is closed so that the lower and upper teeth almost meet.
